column3: A former Amazon engineer created an online petition to urge Washington lawmakers to pass the SB 5130 bill. This bill would mandate employers to provide workers with access to their personnel files and internal rankings for increased transparency. While the bill is stalled, several tech workers will testify on it in the next legislative session.

Thirty-four members of Activision Blizzard Studios have formed a union supported by the CWA. The members have requested for Activision Blizzard to voluntarily recognize it. Activision Blizzard responded that they are “carefully considering” it. Unionization efforts have started in response to poor workplace conditions and issues of sexual harassment.

After two years of organizing, Nava PBC workers formed Nava United in partnership with OPEIU. Besides adding stability and benefits, union organizers hope that this effort will “increase pay transparency, equity, employee retention and attract new talent.” They are currently seeking voluntary recognition.
column9: white collar workers,contract workers,inhouse workers,knowledge workers

column3: Workers at Nava PBC have joined together with a supermajority of their colleagues to form Nava United. Workers at Nava help to build accessible platforms for vital government services (like the DOJ's civil rights portal, medicare and medicaid services, and more), and more. They are forming a union to improve their working conditions and strengthen the work they do at Nava.

In response to new leadership and business restructuring that led to 2,800 employees being fired, terminated Peloton employees (who were allowed to attend the meeting) flooded the chat box of the virtual Q2 earnings call with complaints about the job cuts and mismanagement. Former employees also began helping each other find new jobs on LinkedIn and a publicly accessible spreadsheet.

Google is expanding its North Carolina offices located in the “Triangle Area” for increased diversity in the workforce. However, workers expressed concern over the workers’ lower salaries and stock equity grants. In a letter, employees asked for increased transparency about regional salary calculations and the removal of the salary cut. Moreover, many workers had relocated to the Triangle Area during the pandemic due to remote work for more affordable living expenses.

The Alphabet Workers Union has also created an open letter that expressed their grievances with the salary in the Triangle Area.

In response, a spokesperson has said that their compensation guidelines in the area exceed the market pay benchmarks and that employees haven’t had a reduction in salary or existing equity grants.
column16: chapel hill-north carolina-usa, durham-north carolina-usa, raleigh-north carolina-usa

column3: Over 400 Salesforce employees signed onto an open letter critiquing the company's decision to launch NFT products citing their harmful environmental impact.

More than 500 Google employees signed an open letter who alleged that the company was retaliating against her after she organized efforts to protest Project Nimbus, the company's $1.2 billion contract with the Israeli military.

Part-time hourly workers who operate AppFolio's property management chatbot (called "Lisa") filed for a union election. They said the workload and message volume have steadily increased over time, while pay has stagnated, this is one of several reasons workers are interested in forming a union. The union organized with CWA, and filed for an NLRB election which began on May 10th, 2022. They won on June 8th, 2022, 42-16.

Workers at Nava PBC have received voluntary recognition for their union Nava United with OPEIU Tech Workers Union Local 1010. They are now the largest union of civic tech workers in the US. Some of their goals are to improve the workplace to be more equitable and inclusive, as well as improve pay and PTO.

Microsoft, SAP SE, and IBM have continued to maintain operations in Russia. In response, groups of workers at these companies have called for them to do more than just end new sales and to instead withdraw completely. Workers also discussed and criticized the companies’ stances in internal discussion forums, with some Microsoft workers even threatening to quit if the company doesn’t exit. Other workers worry about the withdrawal’s potential effect on civilians.

In response to Activision Blizzard lifting its vaccine mandate, A Better ABK announced that employees will walk out in protest. Their demands are to reverse the lifting of the vaccine requirement, to allow remote work permanently, and to allow each individual employee to decide whether to work remotely or in person. 

As of 4/1/22, Activision Blizzard is operating under a voluntary return to office policy, and each studio will have its own policies regarding the vaccine mandate.

A group of Amazon workers disrupted a Pride Month event at HQ in Seattle to protest the company's sale of anti-trans books. The group, No Hate at Amazon, demanded that the company stop producing and selling books that the group says are harmful to transgender youth.
Kickstarted United win first contract.

Google executives abruptly canceled an employee-organized event about caste bias in April said the company's top diversity officer during a monthly all-hands meeting on Thursday. Employees bombarded executives during the all-hands meeting with questions about addressing caste discrimination and why the anti-bias talk had been pulled. Three people who were present shared an audio recording of the meeting with Business Insider. Tanuja Gupta, the event's organizer and a senior manager at Google News, had sent an email announcing she was quitting Google because of the company's reaction.
Nine members of Axon's AI ethics board resigned after the company said it would develop Taser-armed drones to sell to schools.
Workers at Salesforce wrote an open letter to urge upper management to stop working with the National Rifle Association. The letter comes after the Uvalde, Texas elementary school shooting.

A petition posted to a decentralized publishing platform mirror.xyz calls for the removal of several Coinbase execs. The anonymous petition was said to have been from employees and asked for a “vote of no confidence” that would remove Chief Operating Officer Emilie Choi, Chief Product Officer Surojit Chatterjee, and Chief People Officer LJ Brock. They were deemed “the most prominent executives who have been executing plans and ideas that have led to questionable results and negative value,” including a controversial performance review system and approach to hiring. The petitioners took issue with Coinbase’s “aggressive” hiring ambitions as well as its decision to rescind offers, which led to negative publicity. The petition appears to have since been pulled down, but Coinbase Chief Executive Brian Armstrong linked to a site referencing an archived version of it while criticizing the initiative Friday in posts on Twitter.

Plaintiffs’ law firms Lieff Cabraser Heimann & Bernstein LLP and Altshuler Berzon LLP announced that Plaintiffs have reached an agreement with Google, in which Google will pay $118 million to settle a class action gender discrimination lawsuit, Ellis v. Google LLC, No. CGC-17-561299, pending since 2017. The settlement covers approximately 15,500 female employees in 236 job titles (“covered positions”) in California since September 14, 2013. The named Plaintiffs are Kelly Ellis, Holly Pease, Kelli Wisuri, and Heidi Lamar. All of the Plaintiffs are women who worked for Google in California in a covered position since September 14, 2013.

Workers at Epic Systems, a medical records software company, protested the company's plans to mandate that all employees return to in-person work in July/August 2020. Two employees created a survey that they then distributed among employees, yielding over 400 responses indicating broad dissatisfaction with Epic's covid response and plans. They sent a summary of the data to Epic leadership, but were ignored. Eventually, Epic walked back their plans after national and local news media picked up the story.

Tech and business workers at the magazine The Atlantic went public with a union campaign. The proposed union would include some 130 members in New York and Washington who are employed in revenue-driving jobs like data analysis, software engineering, graphic design for sponsored content, sales, marketing and customer service. They won union recognition with a card count on September 2, 2022. They joined the NewsGuild union (CWA).

Over 650 Google employees signed a petition organized by the Alphabet Workers Union calling on the company to extend abortion-related health benefits to contractors and better protect user privacy in the wake of a Supreme Court decision overturning Roe v. Wade in June. Google announced after the Dobbs decision came down that health insurance would cover out-of-state medical procedures and that they could apply for relocation without justification, but that these benefits do not extend to TVCs (temporary, vendor, or contract workers). This petition demanded the benefits be extended to TVCs and also add seven additional sick days, for travel purposes for out of state procedures. The petition also demands that Google never save Google searches related to abortion access or hand them over to law enforcement.
